body_markdown:
[Back to All](https://docs.castle.io/changelog)


Added


You can now see which supported AI agents and browser automation tools are interacting with your application. Castle returns their identity in a new top-level` agent` object, including the agent's name, operator, category, and how it was identified.


Castle uses verified Web Bot Auth signatures, browser fingerprints, and recognized user-agent strings. Identification is separate from risk scoring and does not change your bot or abuse scores or existing enforcement decisions. A verified signature confirms the signer, not that a request is safe.


For signature verification, forward the incoming` Signature-Input` ,` Signature` ,` Signature-Agent` , and original` Host` headers in` context.headers` . See[AI agent identification](https://docs.castle.io/docs/ai-agent-identification) for response fields and integration details.


Example API response:


```text
{
"agent": {
"name": "ChatGPT agent",
"operator": "openai",
"category": "ai_agent",
"identified_by": ["web_bot_auth"]
}
}
```
